title: Trace-driven kernel sampling notes and hypotheses
body:
Purpose:

Capture a lightweight, trace-driven approach to sampling kernel-level behavior and kv-cache interactions to reproduce intermittent latency regressions we've seen in November/December 2024. This is a working note: rapid experiments, hypotheses, and short recipes for SRE/eng to run in CI and on repro clusters.

Context / motivation:
- Multiple customer incidents where p95/p99 token latency jumped by 20-60% for short windows under mixed chat load (seq len mix and embedding background jobs).
- Existing microbench harnesses exercise single kernels or steady-state load; they do not capture bursty prefix reuse and cross-request KV cache effects.
- We need a reproducible, low-overhead trace-slicing flow to create targeted microbench workloads that mirror production call patterns (prefix reuse, repeated roles, function calling bursts).

High-level approach:
1) Use production traces (sampled) and an offline synthesizer to convert request traces into microbench profiles: sequence-length distribution, per-request token counts, prefix overlap graphs, and worker routing metadata (model variant, quantization mode).
2) Attach kernel-level sampling at three points: scheduling decision time, kernel launch time, and kv cache lookup path. Lightweight stack/unwind + perf counters.
3) Feed synthesized profiles into the existing harness but with two additions: a) KV cache warm/cold schedule generator (controls eviction patterns), b) scheduling jitter injector (simulate overloaded scheduler that delays batches by X ms).

Trace slicing & profile generation (recipe):
- Input: 1 hour of sampled traces (trace rate ~1 in 1000 requests) from prod region eu-west-1. Use trace extractor script to pull only LLM generation spans.
- Slice by user-session id and by model-variant tag. For each slice compute: token_histogram (buckets: 1-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513+), prefix_overlap_matrix (N x N of Jaccard scores), and kv_cache_access_density (ratio of requests that hit prefix cached segments).
- Output: profile.json (fields flattened for this doc: sequence_buckets, overlap_pairs, kv_hit_rate).

Sampling protocol (kernel-level):
- Sampling points: scheduler_decision, kernel_enqueue, kv_lookup_enter, kv_lookup_exit.
- Method: combined perf_event counters + light stack sampling (async-signal based) to record top-3 frames. Keep payload < 200B per sample to avoid perturbing latency.
- Rate: adaptive: 1 sample per 10k requests baseline, increase to 1 per 1k during observed p95 spikes.

KV cache experiment matrix (quick overview):
- Baseline: no eviction, full warm cache (replicate best-case).
- Eviction sweep: LRU eviction with TTLs of [30s, 120s, 300s]; record p50/p95/p99 tokens.
- Cold-start bursts: simulate 10% of requests with TTL reset (evict N most-recent entries) to mimic GC/rolling restarts.
- Cross-worker contention: set cache affinity to simulate inter-worker misses (hash skew).
- Metrics: cache_hit_rate, avg_kv_lookup_ms, backend_kernel_load_ms, end_to_end_token_latency_ms.

Observed anomalies (from initial run 2024-11-20 snapshot):
- Pattern A: sudden p99 jump correlated with kv_lookup_exit samples showing long tail in remote_memcpy (NVLink) frames. Hypothesis: oversized KV entries (long prefix contigs) causing fallback to remote transfers when local GPU memory fragmented.
- Pattern B: p95 spikes coincident with scheduler_decision samples that show long syscalls (epoll_wait) and then a cluster of enqueue events; hypothesis: rare thread preemption + bursty IO for embedding jobs causing scheduling jitter.
- Pattern C: small but reproducible p50 regression when using kernel variant K-quantized-v2 under seq len 129-512; profiler shows extra memcpy in kernel_enqueue path.

Immediate hypotheses to validate (ranked):
1) KV entry fragmentation: large contiguous prefix objects lead to remote memcpy on eviction and long tail; validate by forcing prefix compaction in cache before bursts.
2) Scheduler fairness bug: default work-stealing interacts poorly with mixed short/long sequences; validate by running with strict FIFO scheduling in a staging cluster.
3) Kernel_variant regression: recent PR switching to new matmul tiling introduced extra host-device memcopy for mid-length sequences; validate with microbench single-kernel call with instrumentation.

Experiment checklist (quick):
- [ ] Generate profile.json from prod traces (use trace-slicer v0.9).
- [ ] Run sampling harness with KV eviction TTL 120s and record full perf samples.
- [ ] Re-run with scheduler mode=FIFO.
- [ ] Reproduce kernel microbench for K-quantized-v1 vs v2 with seq lengths [64, 256, 512] and measure memcpy counts.
- [ ] Upload sample logs to /srv/perf-artifacts/trace-sampling/<run-id>/ and link in ticket.

Quick commands (working examples):
- Extract traces: python tools/trace_slicer.py --in s3://prod-traces/eu-west-1/2024-11-19 --out profile.json --sample-rate 0.001 --filter-span gen
- Run harness with profile: ./harness/run_profile.sh --profile profile.json --kv-ttl 120 --scheduler jitter:5ms --sample-rate 0.001 --outdir /tmp/run-001
- Collect perf: ./tools/collect_perf.sh --pid $(cat /tmp/run-001/worker.pid) --points scheduler_decision,kernel_enqueue,kv_lookup --rate adaptive --out /tmp/run-001/perf

Metrics to collect (CSV-friendly):
- run_id, profile_id, kv_ttl_s, scheduler_mode, sample_rate, cache_hit_rate, avg_kv_ms, p50_token_ms, p95_token_ms, p99_token_ms, kernel_memcpy_count, remote_memcpy_count

Trace snippet example (flattened for readability):
- trace_id: 7f9a2c, user: anon, model: redwood-13b-q4, seq_len: 312, prefix_hit: true, kv_hits: [seg#12, seg#14], sampler_points: [scheduler_decision: 2024-11-19T12:02:01.345Z, kernel_enqueue: 2024-11-19T12:02:01.358Z, kv_lookup_enter: 2024-11-19T12:02:01.358Z, kv_lookup_exit: 2024-11-19T12:02:01.402Z], observed_latency_tokens_ms: 2.1

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Keep sampling payload small; the last thing we want is instrumentation noise producing false positives.
- When reproducing NVLink memcpy, ensure the test cluster has same GPU topology as production (A100-80GB NVLink mesh).
- For local microbench runs use --isolated-cgroup to prevent background embedding jobs from skewing queueing behavior.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we have a way to force prefix compaction in the kv cache without client-facing behavior changes? If not, consider a server-side compaction job (low-priority).
- Could the scheduler jitter be caused by syscalls in the mmap path (I/O for shared checkpoint reads)? Need a syscall trace around scheduler_decision samples.
- Should we add a low-overhead binary sensor at kernel_enqueue that counts memcpy ops per invocation (aggregated counters)? Pros: cheap signal. Cons: requires kernel change and rollout.

Action items:
- Ethan: run FIFO scheduling experiment against profile v2024-11-19 and upload CSVs (due 2024-09-25).
- Sofia: instrument kernel_enqueue to expose memcpy counter in dev build and run microbench (due 2024-10-02).
- Noah: validate NVLink repro cluster topology and script a compaction job (due 2024-10-05).

Appendix: reproducibility tips
- Always run with the same CPU governor and perf_event sampling config used in prod: governor=performance, perf_event_freq=400.
- Use deterministic RNG for synthetic token generation in the harness (seed=42).
- Keep a copy of the exact container image (sha256) and record it in CSVs.

If this doc helps reproduce anything, paste links to the results into JIRA-RT-312 and tag me (Maya).
